newsitem.title: Singapore: Asian crude - North Asian demand provides support.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - North Asian demand provides support.

text.p: Heavy Asian crudes held steady on demand from China and Japan, traders said on Wednesday.
Limited supplies of Minas were now available for July, with only two shosha and an equity producer heard holding barrels.
Most shosha had committed their July Minas cargoes to Japanese utilities early in the month, while over 500,000 barrels were sold to China, traders said.
The latest Minas deal was probably from a shosha to an Australian refiner around ICP +25 cents per barrel, they said.
Rumours were rampant about July light crude deals done at low levels.
An Indonesian affiliate rumoured sold its 300,000 barrels of July Belida to a shosha at ICP +18, compared to Belida deals done at ICP +50 very early in the month.
July Dulang was also heard sold by a shosha at OSP -15/20.
But traders said the levels reflected the market weakness.
Ample supplies, including Bontang Mix, Kutubu, Tapis, Barrow Island, Harriet and even New Zealand Maui condensate were still on offer for July.
August trading for Oman and Abu Dhabi crudes was thin, as traders focused more on the outcome of the Indian monthly crude tender which closed Wednesday morning.
Apart from talk that Dubai was offered by a European major, a Wall Streeter and a Malaysian trading company, details of the tender offers were very sketchy.
August Dubai was heard sold by a European major to a Japanese refiner at whole month quotes -8 cents.
August Masila could have been sold by a trader at OSP +13/14, while a cargo of Al-Shaheen heard sold by an equity holder at Dubai -40.
Bangchak is expected to issue a tender next week to buy August Middle East and Far East crudes, said a refinery source.
